mitochondrial flicker is directly related to focal sarcoplasmic release of calcium, suggesting a tight spatiotemporal coupling between these two intracellular organelles.
transient mitochondrial depolarizations in rat ventricular myocytes reflect focal sarcoplasmic calcium release.
mitochondrial calcium uptake is tightly linked to focal SR release events, and this coupling may be important for regulating SR function.

calcium signaling in cardiac myocytes and the coupling of SR and mitochondrial calcium release.
the relationship between mitochondrial calcium uptake and mitochondrial membrane potential in single cardiomyocytes and the mechanisms underlying mitochondrial depolarization.
the role of calcium in the regulation of cardiac contraction and energy metabolism.

the mitochondrial flickers reflect the local release of calcium from the SR and that the flickers are associated with the uptake of calcium by mitochondria.
focal SR calcium releases result in calcium microdomains that are large enough to promote local mitochondrial uptake.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mitochondrial flicker represents focal release of calcium in the SR and that this is the mechanism by which SR calcium release is coupled to mitochondrial calcium uptake.
the SR calcium release is tightly regulated by the mitochondrial calcium uptake.
focal SR calcium releases result in calcium microdomains that are sufficient to promote local uptake of calcium by nearby mitochondria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondria in cardiomyocytes are highly dynamic, with local changes in calcium concentration and mitochondrial membrane potential.
the SR is a major source of mitochondrial calcium and, therefore, the SR plays an important role in regulating mitochondrial function.
mitochondria are highly responsive to local changes in calcium concentration, even when the changes are very small and transient.
